sources.note: Family-level only: sec. 9.9.4.1 '(i) probably all Kordofanian languages are tone languages (with generally two tone levels, high (H) and low (L))'. Werni (= Warnang) listed among ten Heibanian languages, 'clearly outliers' with Ko; a few tone-marked Werni forms cited; nothing on stress; nothing Werni-specific on prosody.

sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number 2235.4.26; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 36.88
sources.note: Group-level, second-hand: "According to Stevenson 'dynamic Stress, accompanied by High or Low tone, plays a greater role than syllabic pitch as such, but is not equally prominent in all languages'. Examples are not marked for tone or stress." No placement rule; Stevenson 1956-57 had no Warnang data (per Schadeberg 1981), so this does not rest on Warnang material.
